value.description: number, string or boolean; an array for in / any_of

note.description: Private label for your own reference.

location.description: Where the error occurred, e.g. 'body.items[3].tags' or 'path.thing-id'

value.description: The value at the given location

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.
examples: Property foo is required but is missing.

errors.description: Optional list of individual error details

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type. This value should not change between occurrences of the error.

type.description: A URI reference to human-readable documentation for the error.

builtin_fields.description: Available on every event; usable in conditions

code.description: Shown ONCE. Give it to the invitee; it cannot be retrieved later.

source.description: Name of an enabled manual source

muted.description: Entities, sources or phrases that suppress matching items

enabled.description: Default false: test first, then enable.

entities.description: Topics attached to every item (members can subscribe to them)

interval_seconds.description: Polling interval for this source (rss and webmonitor)

conditions.description: All conditions must hold for an item to be delivered

kind.description: entity: matches event entities; keyword: whole-word phrase in title/summary; source: events from a source id

types.description: Only these event types (empty = all types)

ticket.description: Single-use; connect to /ws?ticket=<ticket> within expires_in seconds

ignore_robots.description: Only with a recorded reason; robots.txt is respected by default.

item_selector.description: CSS selector matching each article block or link, e.g. 'div.news-item' or 'h3 a'

link_selector.description: Relative to the item. Default: the first link.

title_selector.description: Relative to the item. Default: the link text.

info.description:
**TradePulse** collects information from many sources, normalizes it into *events*, and delivers
**the items relevant to you** in one live feed, with automatic alerts. Access is **invite-only**.

## Quick start (5 minutes)
1. **Get an invite code** from an administrator (looks like `tp_inv_…`). Codes are single-use and expire.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/register` with your email, a password (10+ characters) and the invite code. The response contains a **token**.
3. Click **Authorize** in this page (or send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request).
4. `GET /api/v1/event-types` shows what kinds of events exist and **which fields you can filter on**.
5. `PUT /api/v1/me/subscriptions` tells the system what you care about (see *Subscriptions* below). **Until you subscribe, your feed is empty.**
6. `GET /api/v1/me/feed` returns recent items. For live delivery: `POST /api/v1/ws-ticket`, then open the WebSocket (see *Real-time*).

## Authentication
- Register or log in to get a JWT; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Tokens expire (default 12 h); log in again to get a new one.
- A **suspended** account is rejected everywhere immediately and its live connections are closed.
- Brute force is limited: authentication endpoints allow only a few attempts per minute per IP (HTTP 429, see `Retry-After`).

## Subscriptions (what you receive)
A subscription says *what to watch*; optional **types** and **conditions** narrow it. An item is delivered if **any** subscription matches, unless it is **muted**.

| kind | matches when |
|---|---|
| `entity` | the event lists that entity (case-insensitive), e.g. `tcs`, `checkout` |
| `keyword` | the whole word/phrase appears in the item's title or text, e.g. `repo rate` |
| `source` | the event comes from that source id, e.g. `status_sim` |

**Conditions** are `field operator value` checks; **all** must hold. Operators: `>` `>=` `<` `<=` `==` `!=` `in` `contains` `any_of`.
Fields come from `GET /api/v1/event-types` (built-in: `type`, `source`, `title`, `summary`, `url`, `entity`; plus each type's own fields).
If an event does not have the field, the condition is simply *false*.

Example: notify me when *checkout* is anything other than up:
```json
{"subscriptions":[{"kind":"entity","value":"checkout","conditions":[{"field":"status","op":"!=","value":"up"}]}],
 "muted":["maintenance"]}
```
Every delivered item has a **reason** explaining which subscription matched.

## Sources
Items come from **sources** that administrators configure (RSS/Atom feeds, web pages read with CSS selectors, manual posts). `GET /api/v1/sources` lists the enabled ones: subscribe with kind `source` and the source's name, or with kind `entity` and one of its topics. Each source is polled on its own schedule; new items appear within one polling interval.

## Real-time (WebSocket)
1. `POST /api/v1/ws-ticket` (with your token) → a **one-time ticket valid for 30 seconds**.
2. Connect to `ws(s)://<host>/ws?ticket=<ticket>` (browsers cannot set headers on WebSockets, hence the ticket). A new ticket is needed for every connection.
3. Messages are JSON text frames:
```json
{"type":"connected"}
{"type":"feed_item","data":{"id":"…","title":"checkout is down","body":"Latency 950 ms","severity":"notable","reason":"Matched your entity subscription \"checkout\"","created_at":"…"}}
```
4. **Reconnect with backoff** when the connection drops (deploys and idle limits close connections). After reconnecting, call `GET /api/v1/me/feed` to catch up on anything missed.
5. Limits: at most 5 simultaneous connections per user; slow readers are disconnected. Close code 1008 = policy (cap/suspended), 1001 = server going away.
The WebSocket cannot be tried from this page; use a client such as Postman or `websocat`.

## Errors
Errors use **RFC 9457 problem JSON**: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"…"}`. Validation failures (422) list the offending fields.
Common codes: `401` missing/invalid token · `403` not allowed (e.g. not an admin, bad invite) · `409` conflict · `422` invalid input · `429` rate limited · `413` body too large.

## Administrators
Endpoints under **admin** require the `admin` role (others get 403). Typical flow: create an invite → share the code → watch its status → suspend/reactivate members → review the audit log.
info.title: TradePulse API

get.description: Newest first. Records registrations, invite creation/revocation and suspensions/reactivations (never secrets).
Status is pending, used, expired or revoked. Codes are never shown.

post.description: Generates a single-use code. **The code is returned only in this response** (only a hash is stored). Optionally bind it to an email and set an expiry (default 7 days, max 30).

delete.description: Only pending invites can be revoked (409 otherwise).

post.description: Publishes one item through an enabled `manual` source; matching members receive it live. Useful for announcements and corrections.

get.description: Health: ok, pending, degraded, failing, overdue (the scheduler missed its schedule: silence watchdog) or disabled.

post.description: Types: `rss` (RSS/Atom feed URL), `webmonitor` (HTML page + CSS selectors; robots.txt respected), `manual` (admin posts). `interval_seconds` is per source (bounded by the platform minimum/maximum). The URL must be a public http(s) address (SSRF-checked). The name is a permanent slug that members subscribe to. Sources start **disabled**: use *Test a source draft* first, then enable.

Fetches the URL with the given settings and returns the first items it would extract (nothing is stored or published). Use it to tune CSS selectors. Fetch problems are reported in the response (`ok: false`), invalid settings return 422.
post.summary: Test a source draft without saving

delete.description: Removes the source, its run history and stored items. Members' subscriptions to it simply stop matching.

get.description: Includes the last 20 fetch runs (status, items seen/new/published, errors).

put.description: Replaces url, enabled, interval_seconds, entities and web settings. Name and type cannot change. Same validation as creation.

post.description: Schedules the next fetch immediately (the scheduler picks it up within seconds). Only for enabled rss/webmonitor sources.
post.summary: Fetch a source as soon as possible

get.description: All accounts with role and status. Password hashes are never exposed.

post.description: Restores access and live matching with the member's saved subscriptions.
Takes effect immediately: API access is rejected, matching stops and live WebSocket connections are closed. You cannot suspend yourself.
Unknown email and wrong password return the same 401 (no account enumeration). A suspended account gets 403. Rate limited per IP.
post.summary: Log in and get a JWT

post.description: Registration is **invite-only**. Provide the single-use `invite_code` you received. If the invite was bound to an email, you must register with that email. Returns a JWT you can use immediately. Failed registrations do not consume the invite.
post.summary: Create an account with an invite code

get.description: Lists every event type with its fields (name and kind: number, string or bool) and the built-in fields available on all events. Only these fields can be used in subscription conditions.
Your most recent delivered items, each with a `reason` explaining why it matched. Use after a WebSocket reconnect to catch up on anything missed.
Returns what you are subscribed to. An empty profile means an empty feed.

put.description: Replaces your whole list (send the complete desired state). Values are normalized (case/spacing) and validated: unknown event types or condition fields are rejected with 422. Limits: 200 subscriptions, 200 mutes, 10 conditions each. Changes apply to live delivery immediately. See *Subscriptions* in the overview.

get.description: Enabled sources with their names and topics (entities). Use a source's `name` in a `source` subscription, or one of its `entities` in an `entity` subscription.

post.description: Returns a ticket valid for 30 seconds and usable once. Connect to `/ws?ticket=<ticket>`. See *Real-time (WebSocket)* in the overview for the message format and reconnect advice.

get.description: Returns 200 while the process is running.
Returns 200 when the service can accept traffic: the database (if configured) answers a ping. 503 otherwise.
